full_details: Mistress Ansell went to church for the house and brought the sermon home with the posset, hot milk curdled with ale, ginger, and nutmeg, in a pewter pot. Gilbert came up as far as the chair with Anne's letter from the Bell, where the carrier came in on Thursday. The children have agreed to outgrow their shoes in the same month. Your father has a cough and is cheerful about it. She would know whether you mean to come at Lent or only to say so. Gilbert told you to answer the last one first. You did not answer it. In the afternoon, still on two bolsters, you struck twenty lines of stale conceit between Berowne and Rosaline and put in a quicker exchange for a tall boy. By night the fever was gone. The songs were not written. The last line was not written.
one_sentence: You kept the bed, drank the posset, and read that the children want shoes in one month and that she would know about Lent.
title: Kept the bed and drank the posset
